page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the t2d server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core metrics placing in the top 25% at 2688.98. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 10692.23 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4962.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, registering 498.39 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and approximately 48.77 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, certain multi-threaded decompression tasks show limitations, as evidenced by a weak multi-threaded bzip3 decompression score of 34.81 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput is also relatively low at 5.44 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2d-standard-4 offers a balanced resource profile, providing dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading at a competitive entry point for non-burstable workloads. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a streamlined option for workloads that rely on network-attached storage. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight language model inference, as demonstrated by its average performance in Redis SET operations and small-model text generation.
